blogs.title: Exuding Deference: The Ninth Circuit Extends Trump v. Hawaii's Reach to Refugee Admissions
blogs.description: This post analyzes the court's application of the Supreme Court's Travel Ban decision to Executive Order 14163, examining how § 1182(f)'s "detrimental to the interests" standard has become a virtually unchecked presidential power. The piece discusses the implications for separation of powers and the judiciary's role in reviewing national security justifications for immigration restrictions.

blogs.title: Shall vs. Authorized: The Battle Over Statutory Mandatory Duties in Section 1522
blogs.description: This post examines the central statutory interpretation dispute between the majority and Judge Lee's partial dissent—whether 8 U.S.C. § 1522 creates mandatory obligations to provide resettlement services or merely authorizes discretionary programs. The analysis explores methodological questions about the weight given to statutory titles, the relationship between "shall" and "authorized" language, and how courts parse provisions that blend authorization with conditions.

blogs.title: Beyond the Threshold: Distinguishing Admission from Entry in Immigration Law
blogs.description: This post explores the conceptual distinction that drives the court's split decision: the difference between the President's broad authority to suspend entry and the statutory obligations that attach once refugees have been admitted. The piece considers how this case draws a line between exclusionary power and ongoing duties, and what this means for the future of the Refugee Act's framework.
